title: Financial actions respect declared available or outstanding budgets
question: Component dues, pending transfer budgets and invoice aggregates have different subjects, ownership and failure conditions.

evidence.title: Repayment components consume no more than their outstanding due
explanation: For non-negative supplied payment and non-negative component outstanding, the inspected component methods apply the smaller of supplied amount and outstanding due, update the corresponding completed/paid field and return the consumed component amount. The methods do not determine the global ordering among loan components.
This separates a component payment cap from the transaction processor’s ordering among principal, interest, fees and penalties; the ordering is not established by these methods.

The cap assumes non-negative payment and outstanding state. Completed/paid fields change before later helpers, whose failure atomicity and persistence rollback were not traced. The inspected tests exercise setter/getter normalization, not these payment methods. Negative outstanding, date-sensitive effects and partial helper failure remain unresolved. Static source reading only; no execution or independent validation. Loan repayment semantics are outside current FinKore Core.

evidence.title: Pending debits consume a configured posted-credit budget
explanation: For an account with the debit constraint enabled, pending debits plus posted debits plus the proposed amount must not exceed posted credits. Pending credits do not fund that budget. A symmetric optional constraint applies to credits. The normal create-transfer path checks overflow and these predicates before inserting the transfer.

Configured account constraints on the normal new-transfer path. Pending/posted counters and pre-insertion guards were read; consensus, persistence atomicity and post/void paths were not audited. Ledger/reservation semantics remain outside Core.

evidence.title: Payment allocation is checked against fresh aggregate outstanding amounts
explanation: Payment validation distinguishes internal transfers and party types, then for customer/supplier references refreshes outstanding data and accumulates allocation by voucher and payment term. It rejects positive or negative aggregate over-allocation using the configured amount precision instead of validating every duplicate row independently.

Invoice/payment domain context, outside current Core. Selected tests assert aggregate rejection and unchanged invoice outstanding, but were not run. Fresh database reads alone do not establish a race-free validation/commit boundary.

evidence.title: Currency-specific validators skip unconfigured currencies and preserve zero bounds
explanation: Django Money selects a limit for the cleaned currency, skips a missing/mismatching currency limit, and treats scalar zero as an effective inclusive bound.

get_limit_value returns None on code mismatch or absent mapping entry; __call__ skips only None and compares cleaned.amount for int/Decimal limits. Min/max use strict < or >, so equality passes. This is selected-domain validation, not a universal available-budget check.

A successfully cleaned Money value and supported limit shape; callable limits may depend on application facts. Nonfinite Decimal admission and validator side effects are not proved by these comparisons. A mapping containing EUR only performs no bound comparison for USD. A minimum of zero still rejects an ordinary negative amount. Neither branch promises FX conversion or an all-currency economic limit. No upstream operation was executed. The conclusion is a bounded static source trace; deployment/runtime-dependent outputs are not certified. This behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core.
